newsitem.title: USA: West Point cadet on trial on rape charge.
newsitem.headline: West Point cadet on trial on rape charge.

text.p: A U.S. Military Academy cadet appeared before a court-martial Tuesday, charged with raping another cadet on a holiday weekend off campus last year, authorities said.

The case is the first of its kind since women began attending the prestigious military school in 1976, West Point authorities said. Cadet James Engelbrecht, 22, is charged with raping a female cadet over the Memorial Day weekend in May 1996 at the home of another cadet in Stockholm, New Jersey.

He faces a general court-martial, which is a trial under military law and the equivalent of a civilian felony trial. If he is found guilty, the senior from Conroe, Texas, could be sentenced to life in a military prison.
In 1976, a cadet was convicted of raping a civilian who attended a dance at the military academy and was sentenced to five years of hard labour and dismissal from the Army, authorities said.

Engelbrecht's defence has said sex between the two cadets was consensual after a party at the New Jersey house, where a group of friends was spending the weekend. The trial, being heard by a panel of Army officers at West Point, was expected to last a few days.
